question.text: How many additional US states will enact bans on cultivated meat before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as the number of additional US states which enact a law prohibiting the sale of cultivated meat before July 1, 2027.

The following states will not be considered for this question:

* Alabama
* Florida 
* Indiana
* Mississippi
* Montana
* Nebraska
* South Dakota
* Texas 

If no new prohibitions on the sale of cultivated meat become law in any additional US state before July 1, 2027, this question resolves as **Zero**.

research:
I found no additional state that has enacted a qualifying ban as of 2026-11-12, so the question currently stands at **zero**. Louisiana did enact a ban in 2026, but it is a trigger law and does not count under the fine print unless its trigger is met. Every 2026 ban bill I tracked in the named states died after passing one chamber or never left committee.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria name no single tracker. The question resolves on whether a state signs a full sales ban into law. The closest current trackers are the National Agricultural Law Center and CSG Midwest.
- 2026-05-05: NALC's 2026 update lists only one 2026 sales ban, South Dakota's temporary one (already excluded). The other 2026 laws are a Mississippi ban on cultivated dairy (not meat), labeling laws in Ohio, Virginia and Idaho, and Ohio's state school purchasing rule. None of these count. [NALC](https://nationalaglawcenter.org/food-law-in-the-states-2026-update/)
- 2026-05-04: CSG Midwest shows the Wisconsin labeling and serving restriction (AB 554) vetoed on 2026-03-27, and Minnesota on labeling only. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-06-01: Louisiana SB 152 (Sen. Fesi) was signed as Act 742, listed effective 8/1/2026. [LA Legislature](https://legis.la.gov/legis/BillInfo.aspx?i=250122) The question quotes language from this bill making it effective only after a final US Supreme Court ruling that such bans are constitutional. An October 2026 tracker says the ban is not in force for that reason. [Tallow, 2026-10-26](https://tallow.app/blog/lab-grown-meat-bans-eight-states-which-expire-what-fda-cleared) I could not open the enrolled Act's text myself (the PDF would not extract), but a committee amendment tying the ban to federal court outcomes was reported. [Soar](https://cpo.soar.com/articles/7870889/Louisiana/Committee-adopts-amendment-tying-ban-on-cellcultured-foods-to-federal-court-outcomes)
- I found no cert petition in the Florida case (Upside Foods v. Florida, 11th Cir. No. 24-13640) after the 11th Circuit upheld the ban on 2026-03-23. My searches may not cover filings after spring 2026. [Duane Morris](https://blogs.duanemorris.com/animallawdevelopments/2026/03/25/lab-grown-meat-meets-the-supremacy-clause-11th-circuit-weighs-in-on-federal-pre-emption/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-26: A tracker counts eight states with bans plus Louisiana's ban on hold. Arizona's HB 2762, signed 2026-06-19, is labeling only. [Tallow](https://tallow.app/blog/lab-grown-meat-bans-eight-states-which-expire-what-fda-cleared)
- 2026-03-12: South Dakota signed its moratorium, SB 124 (excluded). The permanent ban, HB 1077, was vetoed and the override failed on 2026-03-30. [SD Searchlight](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/03/11/governor-signs-lab-grown-meat-moratorium-property-protections-crypto-national-security-bills/)
- 2026-02-24: South Carolina H.5096, a full ban, passed the House 110-0 but was only referred to Senate Agriculture, with no further action. The 2025-26 session has ended. [SC Statehouse](https://www.scstatehouse.gov/billsearch.php?billnumbers=hb5096)
- 2026-02-16: West Virginia HB 4462 passed the House on 2/13 and was sent to Senate Agriculture, which was its last action. Senate bills SB 225 and SB 932 stayed in committee. [WV Legislature](https://www.wvlegislature.gov/Bill_Status/Bills_history.cfm?input=4462&year=2026&sessiontype=RS&btype=bill)
- 2026-02-02: Oklahoma introduced ban bills SB 2116 and SB 2121. I found no evidence either advanced. In 2025 the House passed HB 2829 72-18, but the Senate let the ban die and Gov. Stitt signed a labeling law instead. [KGOU](https://www.kgou.org/2025-05-19/oklahoma-passes-meat-labeling-law-for-different-protein-products)
- 2026-01: In Georgia, SB 415 stayed in committee, and HB 201 is listed as dead (2026-04-02). [BillTrack50](https://www.billtrack50.com/billdetail/1812498)
- Tennessee shelved proposed bans earlier. [KOMO](https://komonews.com/news/nation-world/lab-grown-meat-isnt-on-store-shelves-yet-but-some-states-have-already-banned-it-florida-alabama-iowa-tennessee-federal-seafood-animal-cells)

## 4. Base rates
- New state sales bans by year: 2 in 2024 (Florida, Alabama). In 2025, 5: Mississippi, Montana, Indiana and Nebraska, plus Texas, whose ban is temporary. 2026 brought South Dakota's temporary moratorium plus Louisiana's trigger law, which doesn't count.
- Pattern: momentum has slowed. In 2026, every ban that passed one chamber (SC, WV, Oklahoma in 2025) stalled in the second chamber. Governors in South Dakota and Wisconsin pushed back with vetoes, and more states chose labeling instead of bans (Arizona, Idaho, Virginia, Ohio, Oklahoma).
- The obvious candidates already have bans: the excluded states are mostly Republican-controlled farm states. What remains are the "considered" states and a few others, such as Louisiana, which now has a trigger law and could try again.

## 5. Other forecasts
- The Kalshi market "Which states will ban lab-grown meat? (Before 2026)" priced Tennessee, Arizona and New Hampshire at 1% each, but it covered a period that has already ended.
- The Kalshi market "Will Trump ban lab-grown meat?" sits at 1%. It is a different question (a federal ban).
- The Manifold market on a state banning animal meat is unrelated.
- I found no market or expert forecast that matches this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2027-07-01
- Most 2027 sessions open in January and end between March and June: Georgia (ends around early April), West Virginia (around mid-April, since sessions after gubernatorial elections start later), Oklahoma (ends the last Friday in May), South Carolina (ends in May), and Louisiana (April to June). The South Carolina and West Virginia bills died with their 2026 sessions, so new bills are needed. Georgia's 2025-26 bills also expire. I found no bills pre-filed for 2027 yet.
- Texas's ban sunsets on 2027-09-01 and Indiana's moratorium ends 2027-06-30. Both states are excluded, but renewal debates there may influence other states.
- Newly elected legislatures and governors from the November 2026 elections take office.
- Louisiana's ban only counts if the Supreme Court rules on the issue on the merits, which looks very unlikely before July 2027. Watch for a cert petition in Upside v. Florida, or a ruling in the Texas case (Wildtype/Upside).

# Cultivated meat sale bans: research notes for the July 2027 question

## 1. Resolution source
- No single data series decides this question. Resolution depends on state enactment records. The most useful trackers are the National Agricultural Law Center's Alternative Protein Laws compilation and its 2026 food-law update. As of its 2026 update, the only new 2026 sale ban it lists is South Dakota's, which is excluded. Its listed end date for that ban, June 30, 2030, conflicts with other sources that give 2031. [NALC 2026 update](https://nationalaglawcenter.org/food-law-in-the-states-2026-update/), [NALC compilation](https://nationalaglawcenter.org/state-compilations/alternative-protein-laws-state-compilation/)
- The criteria link Louisiana SB 152 as an example of a trigger law. It says the ban takes effect only after a US Supreme Court ruling, so it does not count unless that ruling happens. [LA SB 152 text](https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1480467)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-11-12 I found no qualifying new state ban. The question is unresolved, and the count stands at **zero**.
- Most legislatures are out of session until January 2027. That means nearly all realistic chances fall in the January to June 2027 sessions.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-10: The only fresh item in the news feed is about the industry, not policy. UK firm Meatly moved production to Imperial College's Grapht Works ahead of a 2027 production run. [Meat+Poultry](https://www.meatpoultry.com/articles/34309-meatly-scales-cultivated-meat-production-in-london)
- 2026-06 (approx.): Louisiana passed SB 152, a ban on manufacture and sale with a Supreme Court trigger. One tracker says it became Act 742, but the official page still showed "Sent to Governor" in the snapshot I saw. Earlier versions contain the trigger, and I could not see the enrolled text. A secondary source says SB 152 and HB 512 were both enacted dormant. Louisiana is **not** on the excluded list, so a 2027 ban without a trigger would count. [legis.la.gov](https://legis.la.gov/legis/BillInfo.aspx?i=250122), [Lifemate](https://lifematetech.com/articles/cultivated-meat-federal-clearance-state-bans)
- 2026-06-19: Arizona enacted only a labeling law, HB 2762. HB 2791, the outright ban with up to 18 months in prison, did not become law. [AZ Capitol Times](https://azcapitoltimes.com/news/2026/01/20/arizona-may-become-first-state-to-ban-lab-grown-meat/), [Tallow](https://tallow.app/blog/lab-grown-meat-bans-eight-states-which-expire-what-fda-cleared)
- 2026-05-29: Louisiana HB 717, a labeling law, was signed. [Daily Intake](https://www.dailyintakeblog.com/2026/06/louisiana-enacts-law-imposing-labeling-requirements-on-cell-cultured-food-products/)
- 2026-04-02: Georgia HB 201 is listed as dead. SB 415, Sen. Dickerson's bill, was last acted on 2026-01-27 when it was referred to committee. I found no later action on it or on HB 986. [LegiScan](https://legiscan.com/GA/bill/HB201/2025), [Legilist](https://legilist.com/states/georgia/bill/1033/sb-415)
- 2026-03-12: South Dakota signed SB 124, a five-year moratorium, after vetoing HB 1077, a permanent ban. The state is excluded. [SD Searchlight](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/03/11/governor-signs-lab-grown-meat-moratorium-property-protections-crypto-national-security-bills/)
- 2026-02/03: Tennessee HB 1155 (Lynn/Pody) went to a House subcommittee and its vote was delayed. A Senate version went to a general subcommittee on 2026-04-01. It appears to have died, but I could not confirm that. [BillTrack50](https://www.billtrack50.com/billdetail/1810587)
- 2026-02-24: South Carolina H.5096 passed the House 110-0 on 02-19 and was then referred to Senate Agriculture. That was its last substantive action, and it died when the 2025-26 session ended. [scstatehouse.gov](https://www.scstatehouse.gov/billsearch.php?billnumbers=hb5096)
- 2026-02-23: Wyoming HB0061, a ban, died in committee. [wyoleg.gov](https://www.wyoleg.gov/Legislation/2026/HB0061)
- 2026-02-16: West Virginia HB 4462 passed the House on 02-13 and was referred to Senate Agriculture, where it stalled. SB 932 also stalled, in Senate Judiciary. [WV Legislature](https://www.wvlegislature.gov/Bill_Status/Bills_history.cfm?input=4462&year=2026&sessiontype=RS&btype=bill)
- 2026-02-02: Oklahoma SB 2116 and SB 2121, both bans, were introduced. I found no evidence that either passed. In 2025 Oklahoma enacted only a labeling law, HB 1126. [WLJ](https://www.wlj.net/ok-introduces-lab-grown-meat-ban-bills/), [KGOU](https://www.kgou.org/2025-05-19/oklahoma-passes-meat-labeling-law-for-different-protein-products)
- Wisconsin: Gov. Evers vetoed AB 554, a labeling bill with a school-service ban. [Lifemate](https://lifematetech.com/articles/cultivated-meat-federal-clearance-state-bans)

## 4. Base rates
- 2024: 2 new state bans (Florida, Alabama).
- 2025: 5 (Mississippi, Montana, Indiana, Nebraska, Texas).
- 2026: 1 that counts as a sale ban (South Dakota, a moratorium), plus Louisiana's dormant trigger law.
- The trend is slowing. The states most willing to ban have mostly acted already. Ban bills often clear one chamber and then die: West Virginia, South Carolina, Oklahoma in 2025, and Arizona in 2024. Governors have also pushed back: South Dakota vetoed a permanent ban and Wisconsin vetoed a related bill. More states have chosen labeling instead, including Arizona, Louisiana, Idaho, Ohio, Colorado, Oklahoma, Iowa and Tennessee's permit system.
- The comparable window is one legislative cycle (January to June). Recent cycles produced 2, 5 and 1 bans.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi's "Which states will ban lab-grown meat? (Before 2026)" market has closed. Tennessee, Arizona and New Hampshire each traded around 1% before it closed, and all resolved No. It does not match this question's window. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxcmeatban)
- Kalshi's "Will Trump ban lab-grown meat? (before 2026)" traded at 1%. It is a federal question, so not relevant here.
- The Manifold market listed (a state banning consumption of animal meat by 2050, 31%) is unrelated.
- I found no Metaculus, Manifold or Polymarket market on this exact question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- January to June 2027 sessions. Bills from 2026 died at session end in South Carolina, Georgia and Tennessee, where the biennium closed, so they would need to be refiled:
  - West Virginia: January to April 2027. Its House has already passed a ban.
  - South Carolina: from January 2027. Its House passed a ban 110-0 in 2026.
  - Georgia: January to April 2027.
  - Oklahoma: February to May 2027.
  - Tennessee and Arizona: from January 2027.
  - Louisiana: regular session in spring 2027. It could revisit the trigger clause.
  - Wyoming, Kentucky, Missouri and others are possible.
- I found no bills prefiled for 2027 yet.
- Litigation: on 2026-03-23 the 11th Circuit upheld Florida's ban on federal preemption grounds. A protectionism (commerce) claim is still pending in the lower court. A Supreme Court ruling would trigger Louisiana's law, but none appears likely before July 2027. [CBS Miami](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/federal-appeals-court-upholds-floridas-ban-on-lab-grown-meat-protecting-states-real-food-law/)
- Texas (ban expires September 2027) and Indiana (expires 2027-06-30) may renew their bans, but both states are excluded.

Gaps: I could not confirm the final 2026 status of Oklahoma SB 2116/2121, Tennessee HB 1155 or Georgia HB 986. I also could not confirm Louisiana Act 742's enrolled text.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 7.5 months, until July 1, 2027. That covers essentially all of the 2027 regular legislative sessions, most of which run January to May or June.

(b) Status quo: zero additional qualifying states. Louisiana's Act 742 is a trigger law tied to a US Supreme Court ruling, which is very unlikely before July 2027, so it does not count.

(c) Base rates:
- 2024 brought 2 new state sales bans.
- 2025 brought about 5, but these were the most receptive Republican farm states, which are now excluded.
- 2026 brought 0 qualifying new states. South Dakota is excluded, Louisiana's law is a trigger law, and Wisconsin's restriction was vetoed.
- The trend runs from 2 to 5 to 0 per year, and the pool of easy candidates has shrunk. A rough base rate for at least one new state in a session year is about 40-50%.

(d) Strongest evidence:
- **Bills stalling (against):** In 2026, every ban that passed one chamber stalled in the other.
  - South Carolina H.5096 passed the House 110-0 on 2026-02-24, then sat in Senate Agriculture.
  - West Virginia HB 4462 passed the House on 2026-02-13, then died in the Senate.
  - Oklahoma's Senate let its ban die in 2025 and chose labeling instead.
- **Governor pushback (against):** South Dakota's permanent ban was vetoed and the override failed (2026-03-30). Wisconsin's governor vetoed a restriction (2026-03-27).
- **Shift to labeling (against):** Arizona (2026-06-19), Idaho, Virginia and Ohio chose labeling laws rather than bans.
- **Legal risk falling (for):** The 11th Circuit upheld Florida's ban (2026-03-23), which lowers the legal risk for new bans.
- **Remaining appetite (for):** Several states still show strong one-chamber support. The South Carolina House vote was unanimous.
- **Bills must restart:** No 2027 bills have been pre-filed yet, and the 2026 bills died with their sessions.

(e) Unexpected scenario: Encouraged by the 11th Circuit ruling and the political appeal of the "Make America Healthy Again" movement, South Carolina's Senate and West Virginia's new session both pass bans in spring 2027. Oklahoma, Georgia or Tennessee follows, or Louisiana passes a non-trigger version. That would give 2 to 3 new states. Alternatively, no state acts and the count stays at 0.

Reasoning: I start from the status quo of zero and roughly a 45% chance of at least one new state in a full session year. I adjust downward because of the clear slowdown in 2026, governor vetoes, the shift to labeling, and the fact that every new bill must restart from scratch. I adjust slightly upward because many states hold sessions in the window, support in some chambers is unanimous, and the legal climate is favorable. Net: about a 43% chance that at least one new state enacts a ban. There is no matching prediction market to anchor on.

Option_B: 0.25
Option_C: 0.11
Option_D: 0.04
Option_E: 0.03

(a) **Time left:** About 7.5 months (2026-11-12 to 2027-07-01). Nearly all of that window is the 2027 legislative season. Most sessions run January to May or June, so the outcome will be largely settled by early June 2027.

(b) **Status quo:** Zero. No additional state has enacted a qualifying full sales ban. Louisiana's Act 742 is a trigger law that depends on a US Supreme Court merits ruling, which is very unlikely before July 2027.

(c) **Base rates:**
- New qualifying state sales bans by session:
  - 2024: 2
  - 2025: 5
  - 2026: 0 new (South Dakota's moratorium involves an excluded state, and Louisiana's trigger law does not count)
- So one of three recent sessions produced zero, and the most recent one did.
- The most receptive Republican farm states have already acted. That shrinks the pool of easy candidates.
- A rough prior for a single session is about 50-60% for zero new states, with a long tail.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-02-24: South Carolina H.5096 passed the House 110-0, then died in Senate Agriculture.
- 2026-02-13: West Virginia HB 4462 passed the House, then died in Senate Agriculture.
- 2025: Oklahoma's House passed HB 2829 72-18. The Senate chose a labeling law instead, and the 2026 Oklahoma bills went nowhere.
- 2026: Georgia's bills (SB 415, HB 201) died in committee.
- 2026-03: South Dakota's governor vetoed the permanent ban and the override failed. Wisconsin's governor vetoed a labeling and serving restriction on 2026-03-27.
- 2026: Several states chose labeling laws over bans (Arizona, Idaho, Virginia, Ohio).
- 2026-06-01: Louisiana chose a trigger law rather than an outright ban. This suggests legislators are cautious about litigation, even after the 11th Circuit upheld Florida's ban on 2026-03-23.
- Overall, ban momentum has clearly slowed, and Senates are the bottleneck.
- No 2027 pre-filed bills have been identified yet.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** The 11th Circuit win and Texas renewal debates give ban advocates fresh legal confidence, and new post-election legislatures take office. South Carolina's Senate (now in a new session) takes up a reintroduced bill, West Virginia's Senate moves quickly, and Oklahoma or Tennessee follows. That could produce 2-3 bans in one session, as happened in 2025. Alternatively, Louisiana could pass a clean, non-trigger ban.

**Reasoning:**
- I start from roughly 55% for zero, given the 2026 stall and the shrinking pool of candidates.
- I keep substantial weight on 1 or more because several states have had bills pass one chamber, and a single Senate flip is enough.
- There is no market matching this question.
- I made only a small adjustment from the prior: there is real prior near-success (South Carolina 110-0, West Virginia), but no concrete 2027 signals yet.
